sources.entry: Claude Code Safety Net by kenryu42 - A coding agent CLI hook that acts as a safety net, catching destructive git and filesystem commands before they execute. Supports Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, Copilot CLI, Kimi Code and Pi.

summary.one_liner: A CLI hook for coding agents that blocks destructive git and filesystem commands and access to secrets before the tool call runs.
summary.what_it_does: CC Safety Net parses what a shell command does before it runs, so wrapping a command or reordering flags does not hide it. It blocks destructive operations such as git reset --hard, git push --force, and rm -rf on dangerous targets, plus install scripts piped from the internet (curl ... | bash), including inside bash -c or python -c. It also blocks access to SSH keys, .env files, ~/.aws, and coding-CLI credentials, both from the shell and from the agent's file tools. Policy can be tuned through a GUI (npx cc-safety-net gui) with Standard, Strict, or Paranoid presets, and extended with official rulebooks for Terraform, AWS, gcloud, and Azure or custom JSON rulebooks. A broken config file falls back to safe defaults rather than stopping the agent. It is explicitly not a sandbox and does not contain processes, set filesystem permissions, or watch network egress.
use_cases: Prevent an AI coding agent from running git reset --hard or force pushes
Stop agents from reading .env files or SSH keys
Share a common safety policy across a team via git
Block rm -rf on dangerous paths during agent sessions
Add custom command rules through JSON rulebooks
Check commands from Node.js code using the checkCommand library API
notable: Parses command structure so wrapping or flag reordering does not bypass blocks
Covers many coding CLIs including Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, Copilot CLI, Kimi Code, and Pi
Shareable team policy committed in a .cc-safety-net/ directory
Embeddable checkCommand Node.js library API without installing the hook
Fail-safe: a broken config falls back to safe defaults
caveats: Not a sandbox: does not contain processes, set filesystem permissions, or monitor network egress
Full documentation is separate from the README; the README is described as the short version
Use @latest with npx; a bare package spec can run an older cached copy
